title: Why pelvic floor training, specifically
body:
The pelvic floor is a sling of muscle at the base of the pelvis. It's usually associated with continence, but the same muscles — specifically the bulbospongiosus and ischiocavernosus — play a direct mechanical role in sexual performance: they compress the base of the penis during arousal, which is part of what keeps blood from draining back out.

That means, unlike most of the levers in this program, it's a muscle you can train directly, the same way you'd train any other muscle — with progressive, structured sets rather than vague effort.

One caveat worth knowing before you start: a small number of men have the opposite problem — a pelvic floor that's already overly tight, often alongside pelvic discomfort or urinary urgency. For that presentation, more squeezing isn't the answer; relaxation training is. The trainer in this app screens for that before recommending a strengthening protocol.
